summary: Prepare employees to recognize workplace AI, check outputs, and escalate concerns. Explore role-based AI literacy training and enrol your team.
lede: AI literacy training helps non-technical employees and contractors recognize AI use and respond thoughtfully to its risks. It builds practical skills for identifying AI-enabled tasks, screening use cases for potential concerns, checking generated content for accuracy and context, and handling personal or confidential data carefully. Learners also practise documenting concerns and escalating them through appropriate workplace channels, while referring technical assessments and detailed legal questions to specialists.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for non-technical employees and contractors whose work involves AI systems, AI-enabled features, or outputs produced by AI. It adapts examples to common functions so you can recognize relevant risks without needing to assess or build AI systems.
audience: Contractors using client-provided AI systems while
modules: EU AI Act Risks and Prohibitions
prerequisites: No technical AI background is expected. You should be familiar with the workplace tasks and digital tools relevant to your role; no coding or programming is required.
